entities.name: Ātman
entities.summary: The eternal Self — beyond body, mind, and death.
entities.description: Ātman is the innermost Self. The Gītā teaches that the Self is unborn, eternal, and untouched by the death of the body — the ground of Arjuna's courage.

seo.title: Ātman
seo.description: The eternal Self in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: The true Self — eternal consciousness beyond body and mind.
concept.meaning: Kṛṣṇa teaches that weapons cannot cut the Self, fire cannot burn it; grief over death of bodies is born of ignorance of ātman.
concept.etymology: Sanskrit ātman — breath, self, essence; the reflexive “oneself”.
examples: Gītā 2 — the Self does not die with the body
“I am the Self seated in the hearts of all” (10.20)
Knower of the field (kṣetrajña) as Self

entities.name: Bhakti
entities.summary: Devotional love of the Divine; a central path in the Gītā.
entities.description: Bhakti is loving devotion. The Gītā presents devotion to Kṛṣṇa as a path of liberation alongside knowledge and action.

seo.title: Bhakti
seo.description: Devotional love as a path in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: Loving devotion and surrender to the Divine.
concept.meaning: Bhakti-yoga is the path of the heart — worship, remembrance, and offering — presented as accessible and supreme in the later Gītā chapters.
examples: Chapter 12 — the devotee dear to Kṛṣṇa
Offering leaf, flower, fruit, or water in love (9.26)
Constant remembrance and surrender

entities.name: Brahman
entities.summary: The Absolute — ultimate reality taught in the Gītā and Upaniṣads.
entities.description: Brahman is the impersonal Absolute. The Gītā speaks of knowing Brahman, becoming Brahman-like (brahma-bhūta), and the relation of ātman to the highest.

seo.title: Brahman
seo.description: The Absolute in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: Ultimate reality — the Absolute underlying all that exists.
concept.meaning: Distinct from Brahmā the creator-god, Brahman is the ground of being. The Gītā links liberation with resting in Brahman and seeing Kṛṣṇa as its personal face.
concept.etymology: From Sanskrit √bṛh “to expand, grow great” — the vast, the Absolute.
examples: Akṣara Brahman — the Imperishable (ch. 8)
Brahma-nirvāṇa — peace in Brahman
Identity and distinction of ātman and Brahman in teaching

entities.name: Dharma
entities.summary: Right order, duty, and righteousness — central to the Gītā.
entities.description: Dharma denotes cosmic and social order, personal duty, and righteousness. The Gītā turns on Arjuna's dharma-crisis on the battlefield of Kurukṣetra.

seo.title: Dharma
seo.description: Duty, righteousness, and cosmic order in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: That which upholds — cosmic order, social duty, and righteous conduct.
concept.meaning: In the Gītā, dharma is both the field (dharmakṣetra) and Arjuna's personal duty as a warrior (svadharma), weighed against compassion and confusion.
concept.etymology: From Sanskrit √dhṛ “to hold, sustain” — that which upholds the world and one's role within it.
examples: Arjuna's crisis: fight as kṣatriya dharma vs. killing kin
Kurukṣetra named dharmakṣetra in Gītā 1.1
Yudhiṣṭhira as Dharmarāja — king of dharma

entities.name: Jñāna
entities.summary: Liberating knowledge of the Self and the Absolute.
entities.description: Jñāna is discriminative wisdom. In the Gītā it is the path of knowing the eternal Self (ātman) and its relation to Brahman, distinct from mere information.

seo.title: Jñāna
seo.description: Knowledge-yoga and wisdom in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: True knowledge — insight into Self, reality, and liberation.
concept.meaning: Jñāna-yoga is the path of understanding: discriminating the eternal from the transient, and seeing the one Self in all beings.
examples: Kṛṣṇa teaching the eternal Self beyond the body
Jñāna-yajña — sacrifice of knowledge (ch. 4)
Field and knower of the field (ch. 13)

entities.name: Karma
entities.summary: Action and its consequences; taught as Karma-yoga in the Gītā.
entities.description: Karma is action. In the Bhagavad Gītā, Kṛṣṇa teaches acting without attachment to fruits (karma-yoga).

seo.title: Karma
seo.description: Action and karma-yoga in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: Action; also the law linking deeds to their results.
concept.meaning: The Gītā reframes karma as disciplined, detached action offered without clinging to outcomes — the path of karma-yoga.
concept.etymology: From Sanskrit √kṛ “to do, make” — deed, work, ritual act.
examples: Gītā 2.47 — right to action, not to fruits
Karma-yoga as sacrifice of action to the Divine
Niṣkāma karma — desireless action

entities.name: Māyā
entities.summary: Divine creative power and the veil that binds the soul.
entities.description: Māyā is the Lord's wondrous power and the illusion that conceals true nature. The Gītā speaks of divine māyā that is hard to cross without taking refuge.

seo.title: Māyā
seo.description: Divine power and illusion in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: The Divine's creative power and the appearance that veils reality.
concept.meaning: Not mere 'falsehood' — māyā is Kṛṣṇa's own energy that projects and binds; crossing it requires devotion and knowledge.
concept.etymology: Sanskrit māyā — art, wonder, illusion, measuring-out.
examples: Divine māyā hard to transcend (Gītā 7)
Guṇas of prakṛti as binding appearance
Refuge in the Divine as the way beyond māyā

entities.name: Prakṛti
entities.summary: Primordial nature — the field of the three guṇas.
entities.description: Prakṛti is material nature. In the Gītā's Sāṅkhya teaching, all action belongs to prakṛti and its guṇas; the Self is the witness.

seo.title: Prakṛti
seo.description: Material nature and the guṇas in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: Primordial nature — matter and energy of manifestation.
concept.meaning: Paired with puruṣa, prakṛti is the changing field of the three guṇas (sattva, rajas, tamas). Actions arise in prakṛti; the wise do not claim doership.
examples: Three guṇas binding the embodied soul (ch. 14)
Lower and higher prakṛti of the Lord (ch. 7)
Field (kṣetra) as prakṛti in chapter 13

entities.name: Puruṣa
entities.summary: Conscious spirit — the knower paired with prakṛti.
entities.description: Puruṣa is the conscious principle. The Gītā's Sāṅkhya and Vedānta strands treat puruṣa as the witness Self, and the supreme Puruṣa as the Lord.

seo.title: Puruṣa
seo.description: Spirit and the supreme Person in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: Conscious spirit — the knower and witness of nature.
concept.meaning: In Sāṅkhya, puruṣa is plural conscious selves amid prakṛti. In the Gītā, the supreme Puruṣa (Puruṣottama) is Kṛṣṇa beyond the perishable and imperishable.
concept.etymology: Sanskrit puruṣa — person, man, cosmic Person (Ṛgvedic sense).
examples: Knower of the field as puruṣa (ch. 13)
Puruṣottama — the supreme Person (ch. 15)
Two puruṣas: perishable and imperishable

entities.name: Yoga
entities.summary: Discipline of union — action, knowledge, and devotion in the Gītā.
entities.description: Yoga in the Bhagavad Gītā means disciplined practice uniting the self with the Divine through karma, jñāna, and bhakti.

seo.title: Yoga
seo.description: Disciplined union in the Bhagavad Gītā.

concept.definition: Disciplined union of the self with the Divine.
concept.meaning: In the Gītā, yoga is not only posture but skill in action, evenness of mind (samatva), and paths of karma, jñāna, and bhakti.
examples: Samatvaṃ yoga ucyate — evenness is called yoga
Karma-yoga, jñāna-yoga, bhakti-yoga as paths
Dhyāna-yoga of chapter 6 — meditation

entities.name: Abhimanyu's Death
entities.summary: Young Abhimanyu enters the cakravyūha and is slain by many warriors.
entities.description: On the thirteenth day, Abhimanyu penetrates the wheel formation but cannot exit. Surrounded, he falls — a turning grief of the war.

seo.title: Abhimanyu's Death — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Young Abhimanyu enters the cakravyūha and is slain by many warriors.

entities.name: Aftermath
entities.summary: Grief, counsel, and the closing of the age after Kurukṣetra.
entities.description: After the war and the Aśvamedha, the Strī, Śānti, Anuśāsana, and Mahāprasthānika movements complete the epic arc — mourning, governance, and the Pāṇḍavas' final departure.

seo.title: Aftermath — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Grief, counsel, and the closing of the age after Kurukṣetra.

entities.name: Aśvamedha
entities.summary: Yudhiṣṭhira's horse sacrifice reasserts dharma after the war.
entities.description: In the Aśvamedhika Parva, the consecrated horse roams under Arjuna's guard; the sacrifice seeks to restore order and merit after the slaughter of kin.

seo.title: Aśvamedha — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Yudhiṣṭhira's horse sacrifice reasserts dharma after the war.

entities.name: Bhagavad Gītā
entities.summary: On the field of dharma, Kṛṣṇa teaches Arjuna — the Gītā unfolds.
entities.description: Between the armies at Kurukṣetra, Arjuna's despair meets Kṛṣṇa's yoga of action, knowledge, and devotion. The discourse is the spiritual heart of the epic.

seo.title: Bhagavad Gītā — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: On the field of dharma, Kṛṣṇa teaches Arjuna — the Gītā unfolds.

entities.name: Bhīṣma's Fall
entities.summary: Bhīṣma falls to Arjuna's arrows, aided by Śikhaṇḍin's presence.
entities.description: After ten days as senāpati, Bhīṣma is brought down and lies on a bed of arrows, waiting for uttarāyaṇa to leave the body.
aliases: Bhishma on the bed of arrows

seo.title: Bhīṣma's Fall — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Bhīṣma falls to Arjuna's arrows, aided by Śikhaṇḍin's presence.

entities.name: Birth of the Kauravas
entities.summary: Gāndhārī bears the hundred Kauravas; Duryodhana rises as their chief.
entities.description: The Ādi Parva narrates Gāndhārī's long gestation and the birth of Duryodhana and his brothers — the rival house that will face the Pāṇḍavas.

seo.title: Birth of the Kauravas — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Gāndhārī bears the hundred Kauravas; Duryodhana rises as their chief.

entities.name: Birth of Kṛṣṇa
entities.summary: Kṛṣṇa is born to Devakī and Vasudeva in Mathurā, then raised in Vraja.
entities.description: The Bhāgavata and Harivaṃśa narrate Kṛṣṇa's birth under Kaṃsa's terror and his childhood in Gokula–Vṛndāvana. On the Timeline this node precedes the Pāṇḍava story he will later guide.

seo.title: Birth of Kṛṣṇa — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Kṛṣṇa is born to Devakī and Vasudeva in Mathurā, then raised in Vraja.

entities.name: Birth of the Pāṇḍavas
entities.summary: Through divine mantras, Kuntī and Mādrī bear the five Pāṇḍava brothers.
entities.description: Kuntī invokes Dharma, Vāyu, and Indra; Mādrī invokes the Aśvins. The five sons of Pāṇḍu — Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva — become the axis of the Mahābhārata.

seo.title: Birth of the Pāṇḍavas — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Through divine mantras, Kuntī and Mādrī bear the five Pāṇḍava brothers.

entities.name: Creation
entities.summary: The opening of cosmic order — Prajāpati, Manu, and the lineages that frame the epic world.
entities.description: Purāṇic and epic traditions place the Mahābhārata within a larger creation cycle — the backdrop for the dynasties of the sun and moon.

seo.title: Creation — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: The opening of cosmic order — Prajāpati, Manu, and the lineages that frame the epic world.

entities.name: Dice Game
entities.summary: Śakuni's dice strip Yudhiṣṭhira of kingdom, brothers, and Draupadī.
entities.description: In the Hastināpura sabhā, Śakuni defeats Yudhiṣṭhira. Draupadī is dragged into the court; the outrage sets the path to exile and war.

seo.title: Dice Game — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Śakuni's dice strip Yudhiṣṭhira of kingdom, brothers, and Draupadī.

entities.name: Draupadī Svayaṃvara
entities.summary: Arjuna wins Draupadī at the Pañcāla svayaṃvara; she becomes wife of the five.
entities.description: At Kāmpilya, Arjuna strings the bow and hits the target. Draupadī's marriage to all five Pāṇḍavas follows Kuntī's word and Vyāsa's sanction.

seo.title: Draupadī Svayaṃvara — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Arjuna wins Draupadī at the Pañcāla svayaṃvara; she becomes wife of the five.

entities.name: Droṇa's Death
entities.summary: Droṇa lays down arms after the false report of Aśvatthāmā's death.
entities.description: Told that 'Aśvatthāmā' is dead — meaning an elephant — Droṇa ceases fighting and is beheaded by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

seo.title: Droṇa's Death — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Droṇa lays down arms after the false report of Aśvatthāmā's death.

entities.name: End of the War
entities.summary: Duryodhana falls; the Sauptika night and aśru close the eighteen days.
entities.description: Bhīma fells Duryodhana. Aśvatthāmā's night massacre and the final astra exchanges seal the war's end; the Strī and Śānti parvas begin the aftermath.

seo.title: End of the War — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Duryodhana falls; the Sauptika night and aśru close the eighteen days.

entities.name: Pāṇḍava Exile
entities.summary: Twelve years in the forest and a year in disguise — the price of the dice.
entities.description: The Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī dwell in forests such as Kāmyaka and Dvaita. Arjuna seeks weapons; pilgrimage and trials fill the Vana Parva years.

seo.title: Pāṇḍava Exile — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Twelve years in the forest and a year in disguise — the price of the dice.

entities.name: Karṇa's Death
entities.summary: Arjuna slays Karṇa when his chariot wheel sticks in the earth.
entities.description: In the Karṇa Parva duel, curses and fate converge: the wheel sinks, Karṇa's arms fail him, and Arjuna's arrow ends the elder brother he never fully knew.

seo.title: Karṇa's Death — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Arjuna slays Karṇa when his chariot wheel sticks in the earth.

entities.name: Kṛṣṇa's Peace Mission
entities.summary: Kṛṣṇa goes to Hastināpura as envoy; peace fails and war is fixed.
entities.description: In the Udyoga Parva, Kṛṣṇa seeks five villages for peace. Duryodhana refuses; the armies gather for Kurukṣetra.

seo.title: Kṛṣṇa's Peace Mission — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: Kṛṣṇa goes to Hastināpura as envoy; peace fails and war is fixed.

entities.name: Lākṣāgṛha
entities.summary: The lacquer house plot at Vāraṇāvata — the Pāṇḍavas escape the fire.
entities.description: Duryodhana's faction builds a house of lac at Vāraṇāvata to burn the Pāṇḍavas. Warned by Vidura, they tunnel out, beginning their years of concealment.

seo.title: Lākṣāgṛha — Mahābhārata Events
seo.description: The lacquer house plot at Vāraṇāvata — the Pāṇḍavas escape the fire.

entities.name: Major Dynasties
entities.summary: The great houses — Sūryavaṃśa, Candravaṃśa, Yadu, and Kuru — take shape.

entities.name: Pāñcajanya
entities.summary: Krishna's sacred conch shell (Panchajanya shankh), sounded on the field of Kurukshetra to declare the battle of dharma.
entities.description: Panchajanya (Pāñcajanya) is the divine conch shell (shankh) of Lord Krishna (Hrishikesha). In Bhagavad Gita Chapter 1 Verse 15, Lord Krishna blows Panchajanya from his chariot beside Arjuna to signal the awakening of righteousness. The conch takes its name from the sea demon Panchajana (Pāñcajana), whom Krishna defeated in the ocean at Prabhasa to retrieve his guru Sandipani Muni's lost son, taking the shell as his sacred shankh. In the Mahabharata, the sounding of Panchajanya filled the hearts of the Kaurava army with terror and proclaimed the triumph of dharma.

seo.title: Pināka

seo.title: Vijaya
seo.description: Karṇa's bow in the Mahābhārata war.
